title: TTL & archival workflow for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics with automated evidence exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need precise controls to set retention (TTL) and archival behavior independently for prompts, model responses, request metadata/logs, and operational metrics. They also require automated evidence artifacts (bundled exports and audit-ready reports) for compliance audits and data residency proof. Current retention settings are coarse-grained and do not produce packaged evidence for regulators.

Goals: Provide a unified policy model and UI/CLI for per-tenant and per-route TTLs, tiered archival (hot/cold/custodian), retention overrides for legal holds, and automated evidence bundle generation on-demand or via scheduled exports. Ensure cryptographic integrity (signed manifests), KMS/HSM compatibility for export packages, and clear audit trail integration with the existing console audit logs.

This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout approach, and success metrics for the first implementation covering: prompts, responses, request logs (headers/latency/errors), and metrics (aggregates and raw metrics traces). Implementation will coordinate with ENG runtime, infra, and security for enforcement hooks and archival pipeline endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI and API can set TTLs per-data-type (prompt, response, request_log, metrics) at tenant and route levels
System enforces TTLs: data older than TTL moves to configured archival tier automatically or is deleted as per policy
Retention overrides: legal_hold flag preserves data independent of TTL until cleared; documented API for customers and internal operators
Evidence export endpoint that produces signed, time-stamped bundles including sample records, retention policy snapshot, and audit log entries
Evidence bundles are stored in region-aware buckets to respect residency settings and support on-prem/private deployments
KMS-integrated package signing and optional envelope encryption for exported bundles
Monitoring dashboards track retention enforcement rate, archival latency, and export generation failures
E2E tests and CI ensure retention rules do not regress existing request processing latencies beyond 3% in P95 paths
implementation_notes: Design a policy model that maps 'data_type' => {default_ttl, archival_tier, residency_region, retention_action}. Use a policy evaluation service (stateless) consulted during write-time to tag data with TTL metadata. Archival worker will pick up expired items and perform per-tenant routing to cold stores or deletion. Evidence export generator composes: manifest.json (policy snapshot), sample_records.csv (first N records matching date range), audit_log_snippets.json (relevant console/audit events), verification.sig (KMS signature). Export endpoint supports ad-hoc and scheduled triggers. Start with S3-compatible cold store; plan for GCS/ADLS connectors. Coordinate with ENG on schema fields required on stored records (e.g., tenant_id, route_id, data_type, created_at, policy_version, residency_region).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag guarded beta for internal tenants and compliance team for 2 weeks. 2) Enable opt-in tenant pilot with customer success on 3 customers representing multi-region and VPC setups. 3) Gradual rollout to all tenants with default conservative TTLs (30d prompts, 90d responses, 365d logs, 720d metrics aggregates) and opt-in shorter retention presets. 4) After 6 weeks of telemetry, flip default flags and publish docs and migration guide.

Rollback criteria: repeated export failures (>3 per day), >5% increase in P95 request latency attributable to retention metadata tagging, or discovery of data loss outside legal_hold rules.
monitoring_diagnostics: Dashboards: retention-enforcement (count expired processed, archival latency histogram), evidence-exports (success/failure rate, average generation time), residency-mapping-violations (cases where data landed outside configured region). Alerts: export-failure SLO breach, archival-queue backlog > 10K, KMS signing errors. Add tracing hooks in write-path to measure added latency from policy evaluation. Logs should include policy_version and enforcement_result for post-mortem analysis.
